function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. The function signature: location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to call the function three times, each with appropriate location and facilities. For New York: facilities: "Reading Room" and "Fiction". For Los Angeles: "Wi-Fi" and "Children Section". For Chicago: "Cafe" and "Reading Room". The facilities parameter expects a single value or array? The type says "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". That seems ambiguous: maybe it's a union of string or array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe" type? But likely they want an array of strings. So we should pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

Thus we need to call function three times. We'll produce separate calls.
